Risk Consulting at AIG 

AIG Risk Consulting helps AIG’s Underwriting teams identify, understand, and mitigate risk to the portfolio and to individual accounts. Our people provide in-depth research and analysis of the issues our insureds face and provide guidance for our Underwriting teams so they can better shape insurance programs. We develop intelligence on historical loss drivers, and we stay on top of the latest emerging risk issues that could become claims activity. We are reimagining how we help the organization manage risk, transforming our operating model and getting better every day about serving our customers and stakeholders.

In addition to Underwriter support, Risk Consultants work directly with clients to identify and mitigate risks to their business such as worker’s compensation, auto or fleet liability, and premises and products liability. When you join AIG’s Risk Consulting team, you are joining a team that is pivotal to developing and executing on AIG’s strategy to be the leading insurance company, standing by our insureds for the next hundred years.

 

 

About the role

The Casualty Risk Consulting team of AIG has an opportunity for a Casualty Risk Consultant in our Chicago office. 

 

This loss control position will work closely with AIG Underwriters to evaluate the operations, controls, and safety culture of various accounts with worker’s compensation, commercial auto liability, and general liability exposures and provide detailed written reports to help underwriting make informed decisions regarding risk transfer. 

 

The position also calls for the ability to work directly with insureds on worker safety programs, premises exposures, and product liability. This includes conducting casualty loss prevention surveys remotely and on-site at industrial and commercial facilities, including:

Identify operational hazards and assess the adequacy of the controls

Analyze of downstream risks of products to users/customers

Identify and assess off-site exposures for various assets within a portfolio

Identify exposures/risk within supply chain

Conduct plan reviews

Evaluate claims data and work with our analytics team to develop insights and potential action plans

Document survey results and provide opinion of risk/recommendations to both underwriting and clients

Provide documentation for underwriting files meeting state regulatory and AIG auditing guidelines

While the position’s focus is support for AIG’s Primary Casualty lines (WC/AL/GL), there will also be opportunities to partner with Underwriting and Risk Consulting personnel in Environmental, Excess Casualty, and other lines of business. 

Travel: up to 25%

 

What we’re looking for:

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree

Minimum of (1) years of experience in at least one of the following areas: insurance loss control; manufacturing or energy industry; or environmental, health & safety (EHS) management.

Strong verbal, written and analytic skills.

Highly motivated and work well independently. The individual must be able to make decisions with and without established guidelines and to provide technical support to underwriters and clients.

Must be able to manage outside contractors/vendors, which AIG uses to conduct some of the on-site and/or specialized worker safety loss control and regulatory tasks.

Must be a team-player able to work with individuals across AIG on diverse projects.

Ability to complete assignments on-time.

Excellent interpersonal and communications skills.

Computer skills with knowledge in Microsoft Office products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Outlook.

Ability to prepare and make presentations to internal and external clients both in-person or on camera with web-based applications.

Familiarity with state insurance regulatory requirements and/or the state and federal litigation system.

Be part of something groundbreaking 

At AIG, we are making long-term investments in a brand-new, innovative Generative AI team, designed to explore new possibilities for how artificial intelligence can be applied in insurance and beyond, and we need your help. 

With the support and investment needed to explore new frontiers in generative AI, you’ll be working alongside talented colleagues, innovating and leading projects that will transform how we manage risk and serve our customers. 

This team is central to our vision of the future and the core of our business offering. To rapidly advance and innovate, we need your skills and expertise to build world-class products. If you’re excited by the opportunity to create meaningful impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you. 

Who we are 

As a world leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions operating in over 70 countries and jurisdictions, AIG’s Global Business Operations & IT team identifies and drives high-quality innovation and cost efficiency in all our processes, systems and operations. The organization ensures we operate as one globally consistent business delivering end-to-end services locally that contribute to our customers’ and AIG’s success.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Data Quality Analyst to support a strategic data quality initiative. This role is embedded within a development team and is critical for proactively identifying and preventing data issues. By ensuring data meets business rules and quality expectations, you will help prevent project delays, increase user trust, and reduce costs, ensuring smoother deployments and better outcomes for both the development team and end-users.

How you will create an impact

As part of the Data Management and Governance team, the Data Quality Analyst will:

Conduct comprehensive data profiling on all source systems (e.g., Snowflake, Foundry, Excel) to identify data characteristics and anomalies.

Identify, analyze, and document patterns, inconsistencies, and rule violations within datasets.

Work closely with development and data quality teams to define, refine, and validate data rules.

Raise, track, and manage data issues that could impact application trust, scalability, or downstream processing.

Provide continuous feedback loops to the development team during the development lifecycle, surfacing defects early.

At AIG, our claims teams are at the heart of delivering on our promise to customers—providing fair, efficient, and timely claims handling across a broad range of insurance products, including Personal Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. Self-motivated and able to work under pressure with a high level of responsibility.

Make your mark in Risk

AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

The EMEA Chief Risk Officer is responsible for ensuring the Risk Management framework for AIG’s subsidiaries operating in the EMEA region and maintaining them at a level that is appropriate for the nature, scale and complexity of its legal entity and producing operations for a business of GPW $5+ billion across more than 20 countries and multiple regulatory jurisdictions.

The EMEA Chief Risk Officer will be a part of the EMEA Senior Leadership Team and ERM International Leadership and may lead engagements as part of this team.

Job Responsibilities

Coordinate Risk Management Key Function holders for EMEA legal entities, Cluster Risk Officers, and ERM Partners for EMEA regional LoBs and functions.

Ensure the maintenance of risk management frameworks and governance systems aligned to AIG’s risk policies, regulatory expectations, and Board and Management support in discharging their duties.

Enhance risk management frameworks proportional to the risks of the region’s clusters, lines of business, and legal entities.

Develop risk culture ensuring an balance between growth, profitability and risk.

Partner with other functions to foster a positive working relationship between teams and relevant regulators.

Support the legal entity AIG Europe’s (AESA) Risk Key Function role by:

Leading regulatory relationships related to ERM and Internal Model.

Ensuring operations at the standard expected of a Solvency II internal model.

Maintaining legal entity internal and external risk reporting.

Addressing actions and findings related to AIG Europe’s ERM department.

Support AESA’s Risk Officers with their regulatory rapport.

Correspond and partner across AIG International, as directed by CRO International, following the Centres of Correspondence model.

Coordinate with International and Global efforts, harmonize of risk management data and technology supporting risk reporting and control.

Liaise with ERM international to ensure and prioritised appropriate service delivery and from global risk functions and shared services teams provide.

Requirements

Strategic risk management - worked at a senior level of risk management and gained a detailed understanding of Solvency II and similar prudential regimes, Risk Assessment, Risk Reporting, Stress Testing etc and other major regulatory initiatives as they relate to general insurance

Extensive risk and industry experience and bachelor/undergraduate’s degree from college or university

Be part of something groundbreaking 

At AIG, we are making long-term investments in a brand-new, innovative Generative AI team, designed to explore new possibilities for how artificial intelligence can be applied in insurance and beyond, and we need your help. 

With the support and investment needed to explore new frontiers in generative AI, you’ll be working alongside talented colleagues, innovating and leading projects that will transform how we manage risk and serve our customers. 

This team is central to our vision of the future and the core of our business offering. We will incorporate best-in-class engineering and product management principles and your guidance and collaboration will be critical to its success. To rapidly advance and innovate, we need your skills and expertise to build world-class products. If you’re excited by the opportunity to create meaningful impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you. 

 

Who we are 

AIG is a leading global insurance organization providing a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services. We provide world-class products and expertise to businesses and individuals in approximately 190 countries and jurisdictions. 

At AIG, we’re reshaping how the world manages risk, and we’re inviting you to be a key part of that transformation. As a Claims IT Business Analyst - GenAI will have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, leveraging and further developing your skills to guide groundbreaking AI initiatives. If you’re looking for a place to grow your career and where your contributions will shape the future, AIG is where you belong. 

 

How you will create impact

The Claims IT Business Analyst will serve as a critical bridge between Global Claims Operations, Product, and Technology to enable delivery of the Claims by AIG Assist (GenAI) program. This role will translate business priorities into actionable requirements, drive process optimization, and ensure GenAI capabilities are operationally viable, compliant, and aligned to the Claims Technology North Star.

 

The analyst will support end-to-end delivery across use cases such as FNOL intake, coverage analysis, document summarization, and adjuster workflow augmentation, ensuring measurable improvements in cycle time, accuracy, and adjuster experience.

What you need to know:

 

Business & Process Analysis

Partner with Claims SMEs (US, UK, and EMEA) to document current-state workflows, pain points, and value opportunities

Define future-state GenAI-enabled processes with clear control points, human-in-the-loop steps, and audit requirements

Quantify business value (cycle time reduction, touchless rates, leakage avoidance, adjuster productivity)

 

Requirements & Delivery

Elicit, document, and prioritize epics, features, and user stories aligned to Product roadmap

Translate GenAI use cases into functional, non-functional, data, and compliance requirements

Support backlog refinement, sprint planning, UAT, and release readiness

Define acceptance criteria and success metrics for each use case

 

Data & Controls

Identify required data elements, source systems, and integration points (e.g., OneClaim, document repositories, legacy in-country policy/claims systems)

Ensure alignment with model governance, privacy, and regulatory controls

Partner with Data, InfoSec, and Legal to operationalize safe GenAI usage

 

Stakeholder Engagement

Act as the single point of coordination between Claims Ops, Product, IT, and Data Science

Facilitate workshops, design sessions, and playback reviews with senior stakeholders

Provide clear executive-level updates on scope, risks, and value realization

 

Adoption & Value Realization

Gather information to help support KPIs and telemetry measurement for GenAI outcomes

Support change management, training content, and adjuster onboarding

Help track benefits against business case and identify optimization opportunities

 

What we’re looking for:

 

Required Experience

7+ years as a Business Analyst in Claims, Insurance, or Financial Services

Proven experience delivering AI/GenAI, automation, or advanced analytics solutions in production

Deep understanding of Claims workflows (FNOL, coverage, liability, payments, litigation)

Strong Agile delivery experience (backlog management, user stories, UAT)

Experience working with cross-functional global teams and senior stakeholders

Demonstrated ability to translate complex technology into business value

 

Preferred Experience

Exposure to LLM-based solutions, prompt workflows, or human-in-the-loop AI

Experience with OneClaim or core claims platforms

Familiarity with model governance, explainability, and regulatory controls

Background in process re-engineering and operating model design

Working knowledge of data concepts (metadata, lineage, quality controls)

 

Key Competencies

Business value orientation with strong analytical rigor

Structured problem solving and process decomposition

Executive communication and stakeholder influence

Ability to operate in ambiguity and drive clarity

Change leadership and adoption focus

The ideal candidate for this senior role within AIG’s Data, Digital, and Cyber Legal Group is a highly experienced cybersecurity attorney with significant expertise managing complex incident response, negotiating and drafting technology and cybersecurity‑related agreements, and advising on regulatory compliance across the financial‑services sector. This attorney will play a key leadership role in shaping enterprise‑wide cyber risk strategy, supporting global business initiatives, and ensuring compliance with evolving regulatory expectations.

The candidate will deliver strategic, pragmatic legal guidance that both protects the organization and enables business innovation. This role requires a sophisticated understanding of cyber threats, regulatory frameworks, operational risk, and the unique challenges facing a global financial institution.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory Compliance & Engagement

Provide sophisticated counsel on U.S. and global cybersecurity regulations applicable to financial institutions.

Serve as a primary point of legal contact for cybersecurity‑related inquiries from financial‑services regulators, including responding to exams, supervisory requests, and regulatory reporting obligations.

Monitor global regulatory developments and proactively advise leadership on required compliance enhancements.

Cybersecurity & Incident Response

Lead legal strategy for cybersecurity incidents, including directing complex, multi‑jurisdictional incident response, coordinating with internal stakeholders, regulators, third‑party forensic firms, and law enforcement as needed.

Develop and refine enterprise incident response protocols, including tabletop exercises, crisis‑management structures, and regulatory notification workflows.

Advise on legal risks related to ransomware, data breaches, network intrusions, vendor incidents, and emerging cybersecurity threats.

Commercial Contracting

Draft, negotiate, and advise on a wide range of vendor and client facing cybersecurity‑related agreements.

Partner with procurement, security, technology, and business stakeholders to ensure contractual controls align with enterprise risk and regulatory expectations.

Strategic Advisory & Cross‑Functional Leadership

Serve as a trusted advisor to the CISO organization, technology leadership, and operational risk teams on cybersecurity and data‑risk strategy.

Promote a positive, collaborative culture within the GLCR department and act as a thought leader across the company and the broader cybersecurity legal community.

Qualifications

J.D. from an accredited U.S. law school and active license to practice law.

10+ years of legal experience, including significant experience supporting incident response and advising on cyber‑risk management for a complex, highly regulated organization.

Deep knowledge of cybersecurity laws, regulations, and regulatory expectations applicable to financial services.

Extensive experience drafting and negotiating technology and cybersecurity‑related contracts.

Exceptional communication, problem‑solving, and crisis‑management skills; ability to advise senior leaders under pressure.

Highly collaborative, adaptive, and business‑focused approach.

CIPP‑US, CISSP, or other cybersecurity/privacy certification preferred, but not required.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Complex Claims Director – TPA Oversight to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

As Complex Claims Director – TPA Oversight, you will analyze and process bodily injury and third-party property damage claims by investigating and gathering information to determine the exposure on the claim; ensure proactive claims handling aimed at the prompt and cost-effective resolution of claims through well-developed action plans. You will determine need for and direct independent adjusters to gather information to determine exposure on the claim and control their costs.

Identify and evaluate coverage issues; prepare comprehensive coverage letters with supervisory review and analysis; retain and provide direction to coverage counsel when necessary.

Assess liability and resolve claim within established evaluation. Maintain diaries and complete tasks within required timeframes as set forth by department guidelines; ensure claim files are timely and properly documented with clear and concise analysis on coverage, damages, reserves, and liability including an action plan for resolution. Process and pay invoices within a timely manner.

Coordinate vendor referrals for additional investigation and/or litigation management. Calculate and assign timely and appropriate reserves; monitor reserve accuracy throughout the life of the claim.

Refer case as appropriate to supervisor and management. Respond to requests or directions in a professional and timely manner.

Attend arbitrations, mediations, settlement conference and trials.

Successfully complete required State licensing examinations and continuing education requirement.

Communicate with all internal business partners including underwriters to make sure underwriting is aware of large losses and industry trends.

Partner with TPA Governance and Relationship Management to help TPA’s and Insureds comply with claim handling and reporting guidelines.

Work with TPA Claims Financial to check the accuracy of TPA financials ensuring alignment with TTPO financials.

What you will need to succeed

7 plus years of General Liability/Auto claims experience.

Experience with complex and high exposure General Liability Bodily Injury and Property Damage claims.

Excellent communication skills (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills.

Advanced experience and capabilities in litigation claims management, including ADR and mediation processes, involving auto/GL exposures.

Strong technical expertise interpreting insurance contracts.

In depth knowledge of claim handling procedures, claims performance strategies, and claim best practices.

Advanced analytical and problem solving skills.

Should also have a demonstrated ability to initiate and champion change initiatives that leverage technology and improve skills in benchmarking.

Creativity in resolving challenging business problems, as well as ability to achieve business goals and objectives is essential.

Corporate Finance - Investment Accounting

The Investment Accounting group at AIG is responsible for the accounting and reporting for AIG's Invested Assets of over $95 billion a comprised primarily of fixed maturity securities and includes private equity, hedge funds, commercial/residential loans and equity securities. In addition, AIG’s derivative portfolio consists primarily of foreign exchange derivatives but also includes interest rate and other derivative instruments. 

The Investment Accounting group’s specific responsibilities include reconciliation of transactional data from various sub-ledgers to the general ledger and ultimately AIG's financial statements as well as all related external reporting for investments (10Q/K, Financial Supplement, STAT Audited Financials and Investment NAIC reporting). The team is also responsible for the implementation of new accounting systems as it relates to invested assets, implementation of new GAAP and STAT accounting standards as it relates to invested assets, establishing the accounting for new transactions or new investment types and management of the risks, controls and AIG audit as it relates to investments and supporting Investment FP&A.

Responsibilities

Execute and support accounting processes related to the monthly and quarterly accounting close to ensure accuracy of AIG’s invested assets data.

Prepare AIG’s statement of cash flows for investments

Execute and support the preparation of certain Investment disclosures for AIG 10Q/K and Financial Supplement. These include all Investment, Lending, Fair Value, VIE Footnotes and Investment MD&A.

Assist in new initiatives for process improvements and systems implementations, in coordination with other areas of the department/organization.

Prepare annual investment related NAIC/STAT reporting exhibits, schedules, and disclosures

Point of contact and support for the various business unit and corporate controllers.

Coordinate with various areas in the organization to develop an understanding of new investment transactions and to provide guidance/support that ensures the accounting results from these investments are accurately recorded in the AIG ledgers across multiple bases (GAAP and Insurance Statutory).

Support management with ad-hoc analytical requests.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance; CPA a plus.

5+ yrs of investment accounting related experience preferred.

Experience in accounting and reporting for investments.

Deep knowledge of financial instruments, including fixed income and equity securities, loans, alternative investments, and more.

Knowledge of GAAP accounting pronouncements, US GAAP and US insurance statutory disclosure and reporting requirements for invested assets.

Ability to work collaboratively with teams in multiple locations

Ability to balance multiple projects at once, to prioritize appropriately, and to approach the work with a sense of urgency and strong attention to detail to produce high quality results in a time sensitive environment.

Team-player mindset geared towards process improvements and the implementation of accounting controls to ensure consistency and data quality of the team’s financial output.

High level of motivation and initiative, ability to work independently, including strong organizational skills.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Comfort level working within a dynamic and complex organizational structure.

Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to maintain relationships at all levels within the organization.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff, peers, and other external and internal audiences.

Computer proficiency with a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

About the role

Lexington has an opportunity for a Senior Production Specialist on the U.S. Builders Risk team specializing in underwriting primary, quota share and excess construction risk opportunities. The Senior Production Specialist is expected to work effectively in an independent manner to successfully manage his/her book of business of new and renewal production along with executing the profitability strategy for the territory’s portfolio. A Senior Production Specialist must be able to illustrate sufficient technical analysis and underwriting acumen combined with marketing and sales skills to meet underwriting goals (i.e., achieve growth targets and maintain overall profitability). In addition, the ability to coach, train and develop current staff to their fullest potential is required.

What you need to know:

As a senior underwriter on the builder's risk team, you are respected for your technical expertise and/or ability to oversee complex programs and processes. You balance the needs of multiple stakeholders, making sound decisions using data, analysis, experience, and judgment, along with a risk mindset. Ultimately, you take ownership for key outcomes.

Produce, underwrite, manage and service a profitable book of business within the team structure.

Utilize underwriter authority in accordance with the published underwriting guidelines.

Handle a portfolio of Master Builders Risk program renewals and new single project business made up of complex risks.

Ability to seek out and partner with internal / external stakeholders in securing new profitable business.

Manage and develop effective producer and client relationships throughout the U.S.

Work alongside business development colleagues to effectively maximize our distribution partner network.

Effectively negotiate and secure policy terms that align with the company directives, especially utilizing new product and service offerings to bring value to the client.

Develop and manage underwriting strategies for both renewals and prospects within his/her portfolio of accounts, including knowledge of the current penetration by product, and specific plans to appropriately manage capacity.

Provide direction and support to less experienced underwriters on new and renewal business.

Proactively foster and develop positive relationships with key customers.

Execute established strategy and work collaboratively with other aligned business functions including claims, actuarial, engineering, operations, analytics, legal and marketing.

Make internal and external presentations as assigned and deemed necessary.

What we’re looking for:

Minimum of 7 years underwriting experience in the Builders Risk or Property.

4-year college / university Bachelor's Degree.

Extensive knowledge of builder’s risk and property forms and wordings.

Strong relationships with retail and / or wholesale brokerage partners.

Knowledge of the builder’s risk market, portfolio management, acquisition and distribution.

Ability to work in a fast-paced environment making quick decisions while adhering to a sound underwriting discipline.

Outcome focused, self-motivated, flexible and enthusiastic.

Strong interpersonal skills with emphasis on collaboration and teamwork.

Proficient working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook is required.

Ready to accelerate your career? We would love to hear from you.

Compensation for this position includes base salary and eligibility for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

At AIG, we are making long-term investments in a brand-new, innovative Generative AI team, designed to explore new possibilities for how artificial intelligence can be applied in insurance and beyond, and we need your help.

Experience setting up E2E Engineering pipeline, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

Are you ready to take the next step in your insurance career with a role that combines commercial relationships and underwriting?

We are looking for a new team member to join our Nordic Accident & Health (A&H) team in Stockholm. Whether you are currently working as an Underwriter, an Insurance Broker, or an Account Manager, this role offers you the platform to develop your skills in a truly international environment.

We are looking for a commercially minded profile who enjoys building relationships and is ready to take responsibility for their own portfolio.

Your day-to-day base will be our centrally located Stockholm office. You will be part of the local Swedish team, but also integrated in our Nordic structure with around 30 professionals across the four Nordic countries.

What’s in it for you?

At AIG, we believe in "freedom with responsibility." We provide the framework and support, but we trust you to structure your day and manage your clients.

Here is what you can expect:

Take ownership of a Swedish A&H portfolio, with the autonomy to develop strategies for profitable growth together with the rest of the team.

Join a social team in our central Stockholm office, while working as a fully integrated member of the wider Nordic A&H team across Sweden, Denmark, Finland, and Norway.

We offer flexible working hours and a hybrid set-up to help you align your work with your personal priorities.

We offer a competitive package including occupational pension, private medical insurance, generous wellness allowance, and a yearly bonus.

5 additional vacation days annually (30 days total) to ensure you have time to recharge.

A culture that encourages learning, with access to our Underwriting University, LinkedIn Learning, and our internal learning platform with both live and at your own pace learning opportunities.

Your impact and responsibilities

You will play a central role in the Swedish market, balancing the daily operations of your portfolio with relationship building. It is not just about technical details; it is about finding solutions that work for our partners.

Your key responsibilities include:

Developing and maintaining strong, commercial relationships with key brokers and clients in Sweden.

Managing the full lifecycle of your accounts – from underwriting and quoting to renewals and servicing.

Collaborating with the Nordic distribution team to identify new opportunities.

Acting as a sparring partner for brokers, ensuring AIG is top-of-mind when they place business.

Handling both local Swedish clients and incoming Nordic and multinational programs.

 

What you’ll need to succeed

We are looking for a candidate with a solid foundation and the right mindset. Relationships are key in this role, together with an analytical and structured mindset.

 

We believe you are a match if you have:

Have experience from the insurance industry – for example as a Broker, Underwriter, or Account Manager.

A commercial mindset and a natural flair for building trust with external partners.

Fluency in Swedish and English (written and verbal).

A structured approach to your work and the ability to work independently.

An interest in international insurance programs and niche products like Business Travel and Personal Accident.

The desire to work in a flat, Nordic hierarchy where we help each other succeed.

How to apply

Send us your motivated CV, and feel free to include a short section on your motivation and fit for the role.

We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We welcome applications in Scandinavian or English. For inquiries, contact:

Risk Consulting at AIG is about teamwork! It is about utilizing your resources, working together to solve real world problems, and making a positive impact on our client’s futures. When asked, “why do we enjoy what we do?” The answer is simple, the people. 

The role of a Field Risk Engineer is core to what we do at AIG, both as a risk management resource to our clients and as a leading global insurance organization. Field Risk Engineers are responsible for working with clients to identify and mitigate risks to their business such as fire, flood, windstorm, equipment breakdown etc. 

A Day in the Life 

Looking for variety and a challenge? Property loss prevention surveys range in size and scope. One day you may be looking at a metal working facility, the next, a university campus. The key to success isn’t about being the expert in every occupancy, it’s about building trust and cross-functional relationships with stakeholders through effective communication. After the survey is complete, it’s time to tap into your strong analytical skills. Utilizing internal and external guidelines, leading edge tools and methodologies you develop loss prevention solutions to any identified hazards. Need that occupancy expertise after all? We have a Technical Integration Group as well as a vast team with years of experience to provide training, mentorship, and collaboration.

Strong communicator (both oral and written) 

Position is expected to travel and attend meetings at various office, field, and construction sites

Travel (~25% overnight) to conduct property loss prevention surveys at commercial facilities

Analyze water supplies and sprinkler system demands to determine water supply and sprinkler system adequacy

Identify and assess the impact of external exposures on a facility 

Determine fire and natural catastrophe loss estimates for a facility 

Conduct consultative visits at customer facilities 

Conduct plan reviews 

Witness fire protection equipment testing 

Document survey results in a data-driven report writing application 

Mentor and train lesser experienced staff

Highly motivated and works well without close supervision.

Ability to complete assignments on-time.

Ability to read construction drawings, diagrams, printed materials

Ability to perform physical activities required for the position (i.e., be on feet and walking 8-10 hours a day, safely work at heights) 

Ability to understand and appreciate safety training specific to numerous workplace and construction hazards

Who we are:

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide financial security.

About the role:

The Enterprise Risk Management function plays a critical role in safeguarding the company’s financial strength and strategic objectives. ERM’s purpose is to lead and drive enterprise risk accountabilities across AIG by identifying and assessing risk; fostering a risk-aware culture; and providing risk oversight and governance, business integration and advisory services, and data driven insights.

As part of the Risk Aggregation and Cross Enterprise Risk team within ERM, the Senior Risk Analyst will support the global risk aggregation initiatives and help manage cross-enterprise risks. This role will also contribute to ERM projects that produce risk insights and drive risk awareness across the organization.

Responsibilities:

Support the identification, assessment, and aggregation of significant risks globally to create a comprehensive, enterprise-wide view of the risk exposure.

Support the design, analysis, and quantification of holistic risk scenarios.

Conduct independent research and support scenario development for key risk areas.

Extract and analyze data from various internal and external sources cross risk categories. 

Summarize and report on risk insights to promote risk awareness and inform risk management actions.

Assist the development of methodologies and reporting for risk aggregations.

Support risk projects including researching, compiling, analyzing and summarizing findings to produce insightful risk reports for senior leadership, as needed.

Collaborate with other teams across functions, regions, and business lines to develop risk exposure assessment capabilities and to drive consistency in risk aggregation approaches.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree with 2 – 5 years of experiences, or an advanced degree with 1 – 5 years of experience in STEM, risk management, insurance, actuarial science, data science or related fields.

Strong Interest and understanding of insurance risk management, aggregation analysis, and scenario design.

Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset, including ability to conduct independent research and deliver results efficiently.

Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

Proficiency in SQL and demonstratable capabilities in GIS (ArcGIS, QGIC, etc.)

Experienced in scripting languages such as Python or R, with the ability to develop independent analytical tools.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to business stakeholders.

Proven ability to collaborate effectively.

Familiarity with risk aggregation tools and data analysis techniques is a plus.

Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles

Maîtrise des outils informatiques pour la gestion informatisée des dossiers de sinistres

The Internal Audit Strategy & Operations team enables the audit function to operate efficiently, leverage data and technology, and deliver meaningful insights to senior management. In this role, you will combine business acumen, audit process knowledge, and analytical skills to enhance how Internal Audit plans, executes, and reports its work.

You will work cross-functionally with Audit Leadership, Data Analytics, and Technology teams to optimize tools, streamline processes, and support execution of the department’s strategic initiatives.

As a member of the Internal Audit Operations team, you will have an exciting opportunity to learn about AIG’s products and services and enhance your knowledge and skillsets as you participate with cross-functional stakeholders including Auditors, Technology teams, Legal and Regulatory teams, Data engineering teams and Internal Audit leadership team.

IAG is seeking candidates who have excelled in previous work experience, possess strong analytical and interpersonal skills, and are enthusiastic about and committed to AIG to contribute to IAG’s mission of being an industry leading internal audit team and key contributor to the achievement of the firm’s strategic goals. We are looking for candidates that are proactive, continuously learn and introduce improved ways of doing things, both to business stakeholders in development of solutions to problems, IAG processes, including the use of data analytics. 

The ideal candidates will be bold thinkers with an entrepreneurial bent and will possess a powerful blend of IQ (technical skills, consistent learning, statistical & financial acumen) and emotional intelligence [EQ] (adaptive communication, empathy, listening skills, challenging with humility). IAG also looks for diverse backgrounds of experience, culture and thought. Successful candidates typically have a global perspective and a record of successful teamwork. You will be part of a large and diverse firm working within a team-oriented environment. You will gain a unique view of AIG, as part of planning and executing on all aspects of the audit process and risk assessment activities and will build close working relationships with business and functional leaders, colleagues across other assurance functions, and fellow team members.

Specific Responsibilities Include:

Strategic Planning & Governance

Support Internal Audit leadership in developing and tracking strategic priorities, KPIs, and departmental performance metrics.

Assist in the preparation of executive presentations and reports for the Audit Committee and senior management.

Research emerging risks, regulatory trends, and best practices to inform Internal Audit’s strategic roadmap.

Assist in driving the annual planning exercise for Internal Audit.

Operations, Operational Excellence & Process Improvement

Manage the centralized Change Request process for Internal Audit.

Evaluate and improve Internal Audit processes, methodologies, and tools to enhance efficiency and consistency.

Document audit processes and technology tools, ensuring effective knowledge transfer across the team.

Develop and maintain Internal Audit policy and procedure documentation.

Data, Analytics & Reporting

Design, build, and maintain reports and dashboards using tools such as Excel, Access, SQL, PowerBI, or similar.

Develop self-service analytics and reporting solutions for auditors and management including weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting.

Partner with the Audit Data & Technology team to implement automation, GenAI, and digital enablement initiatives.

Analyze audit and risk data to identify trends, insights, and process improvement opportunities.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

Liaison with vendor teams and resources to onboard and support their transition to Internal Audit.

Provide training, guidance, and support to audit teams on new tools, processes, or analytics solutions.

Present findings, insights, and recommendations in a clear and concise manner to senior stakeholders.

Qualifications

4 plus years of relevant experience in Internal Audit, Risk Management, or Audit Operations, or analytics experience within a financial or corporate environment.

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in data management, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, or related discipline.

Experience developing applications and reports using Excel, Access, COGNOS, QlikView, SQL, VBA, or similar tools.

Strong understanding of audit methodology, data analytics, and process improvement.

Knowledge of various financial industry business functions and risk/audit concepts.

Excellent communication skills—both written and verbal—with the ability to educate and influence diverse stakeholders.

Strong attention to detail, time management, and the ability to prioritize multiple projects effectively.

Proven ability to document processes, share knowledge, and enhance team capabilities.

Exhibits professional skepticism, curiosity, and a team-player mentality while holding self-accountable for team success.

How you will create an impact

Key accountabilities will include but not limited to:

1.Chief Finance Officer

Strategic Financial Leadership & Business Partnership: 

Serve as the primary financial advisor to China CEO, Board of Directors, and senior management on all financial matters.

Participate in strategic planning and other major operational and risk management activities.

Develop and execute the company's long-term financial strategy, including capital and business planning.

Lead the mid/long-term planning, annual budgeting, and quarterly forecasting processes.

Provide financial insights and analysis to support underwriting, pricing, claims, and distribution strategies and decisions.

Financial Reporting, Control & Compliance: 

Ensure the timely and accurate preparation of all financial statements in accordance with PRC GAAP and Group reporting standards.

Assume the regulatory required role of the Financial Responsible Person of the insurance entity.

Treasury, Capital & Solvency Management:

Proactively manage capital and solvency of the insurance entity to meet or exceed regulatory capital requirements.

Analyze underwriting results, claims trends, and expense ratios to identify opportunities for performance improvement.

Team Leadership & Organizational Development:

Foster a culture of continuous improvement, professional excellence, and cross-functional collaboration.

Manage the portfolio to contribute positively to the company's overall solvency position.

 Ensure the investment portfolio provides sufficient liquidity to meet claim payments and other operational cash flow needs, especially in stress scenarios.

Experience of engaging with senior management level and local regulatory authorities.

Advance presentation and communication skills.

Good interpersonal skills.

Ability to explain complex financial information to non-financial colleagues.

Able to work independently and proactively.

Able to work cohesively in a matrix structure managing experienced senior finance professional.

Goal oriented and well-organized, with the ability to develop and manage disciplined processes.

Problem solving and analytical skills.

Dealing with ambiguity.

A desire to improve process efficiency and deliver a high-quality work product.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as the Regional Multinational Service Delivery Manager - Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Who we are:
American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security.

Get to know the business 
General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services – focused on helping to manage risk for commercial and personal customers. We offer a broad range of products through a diversified, multi-channel distribution network, including one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks.

Multinational
AIG’s Multinational business is an exciting area within General Insurance that will challenge you every day to explore new opportunities for our clients worldwide. As a trusted advisor, you will tailor multinational insurance solutions for our global clients, empowering them to operate across borders with confidence and consistency. Partner with a dynamic, global team of experts, including underwriters, risk engineers, and analytics and claims professionals, to design, implement and service multinational insurance programs. This includes issuing timely policies, providing regulatory advice, sharing local knowledge, supporting efficient money movement capabilities and deploying large fronted limits. AIG Multinational professionals have the diverse skills and expertise necessary to deliver customized, compliant and seamless solutions that support our clients’ risk management objectives. With in-depth knowledge of local markets, practices and regulations, Multinational provides world-class insurance solutions and helps clients successfully navigate their cross-border risks, wherever in the world their businesses take them.

How you will create an impact
The Regional Multinational (MN) Service Delivery Manager will work to implement the MN Business Model, agreed MN Organizational Alignment, Resource & Efficiency Plans and globally consistent MN processes, roles & responsibilities, procedures, controls, performance metrics throughout all countries / territories within assigned region and across the AIG Network (including non AIG countries), partnering with relevant stakeholders such as in country local leadership teams, Fac desk underwriters, MN Operations & Training, Quality, Risk & Compliance colleagues to meet targeted standards in terms of quality, customer service, compliance, and timeliness, all of which underpin AIG’s Multinational Value Proposition.

The position will be responsible to coordinate servicing efforts for PO´s and IO´s but also Network partner territories - including complicated negotiations, regulations, relationships and agreements and external parties like local reinsurers in territories such as Argentina, Venezuela, Chile, Colombia, etc.

In addition to the service delivery discipline the role will require development of thought leadership strategies across all countries such as podcasts, videos, and social media updates to embrace the MN strategy “Telling the MN story”.

The Regional Multinational Service Delivery Manager, will report directly to the Head of Multinational (LAC)

Detailed Responsibilities:

Promote a customer-focused environment. Ensure all regional Producing Office (PO), Issuing Office (IO) and network partners (NP) service expectations and Service Level Agreement (SLA’s) are met or exceeded in accordance with mandated processes and operating procedures.

Drive AIG Network Integration (IO/PO/Network Partners (NP)) within broader AIG Network Optimization strategy. Evaluate regional service delivery resources according to capacity requirements.

Drive continuous improvement across the region in partnership with the AIG LAC & MN Operations colleagues. Solicit feedback from management and staff and socialize ideas. Evaluate recommended changes and implement new procedures to improve the region’s operations.

Support the Head of MN to transition the MN team to a more strategic and external team by developing the local frameworks to operate with complete focus on service excellence and total adoption / usage of MN platforms such as Power BI, Qlickview, etc.

Actively engage and participate in country, regional and global multinational initiatives.

Resolve service delivery issues by engaging with other parties within the AIG network as required.

Evaluate and recommend changes in processing methods and procedures; develop, recommend and implement new processes, procedures and establish control framework.

Ensure the LAC Region meet and exceed the standards in terms of quality, customer service, compliance, and timeliness in servicing Multinational Accounts.

Drive and support growth strategies such as Fac desk accelerated growth plan (FLAG), Global fronting expansion strategies as well as governance/distribution or contributing to strategies such as the NP’s expansion. Act as liaison of the Fac desk team.

Develop a dedicated NP service delivery strategy for 36 NPs, 44 relationships, and 8 IO’s and 4 PO’s – considering a high-level complexity around these territories in terms of reinsurance, regulations, etc.

Coordinate and escalate system, operations and Service delivery country issues.

Lead System, Operations and Service delivery Multinational initiatives and projects.

Track and report efficiency of the Multinational teams; recommend corrective action in response to service delivery issues; ensure complaints from within the AIG network or internal departments and legal inquiries are addressed within established guidelines and protocols.

Apply analytics for operational performance measurement, benchmarking and competitive analysis around key areas, to include: Policy Issuance, Rejection Analysis, Booking Analysis, Operating model effectiveness.

Maintain strong and effective relationships with key business stakeholders to ensure that MN service delivery meets expectations. Foster close partnership with underwriting, risk management, distribution and claims teams to provide excellent customer focus that understands and meets client’s needs.

Partner with relevant MN Training, Quality, Risk & Compliance colleagues to identify, report, review and communicate relevant issues, challenges, risks, opportunities and training needs.

Complete special projects as assigned.

Ensure continuous velocity of Multinational requests across the Region to directly enhance our ability to deliver a superior experience, improve effectiveness and enhance Multinational workforce efficiency.

Experience in Commercial – Personal Insurance / Global Fronting, International Business Environment and Insurance Regulation

Proven background in dealing with multinational and Captive Fronting programs at all levels with an intimate knowledge of regulatory, technical, and processing requirements.

Nordic Integration: You get the best of both worlds – a strong local professional environment in Copenhagen and a direct reporting line to Sweden, ensuring a true Nordic perspective.

Complex Portfolio: You will work with diverse and complex clients, giving you the opportunity to utilize and further develop your technical underwriting skills.

Autonomy: We trust you to manage your own portfolio, negotiate with brokers, and make sound underwriting decisions with support from the team.

How you will create an impact

Identify and evaluate coverage issues; prepare comprehensive coverage letters with supervisory review and analysis; retain and provide direction to coverage counsel when necessary.

Assess liability and resolve claim within established evaluation. Maintain diaries and complete tasks within required timeframes as set forth by department guidelines; ensure claim files are timely and properly documented with clear and concise analysis on coverage, damages, reserves, and liability including an action plan for resolution. Process and pay invoices within a timely manner.

Coordinate vendor referrals for additional investigation and/or litigation management. Calculate and assign timely and appropriate reserves; monitor reserve accuracy throughout the life of the claim.

Refer case as appropriate to supervisor and management. Respond to requests or directions in a professional and timely manner.

Attend arbitrations, mediations, settlement conference and trials.

Successfully complete required State licensing examinations and continuing education requirement.

Communicate with all internal business partners including underwriters to make sure underwriting is aware of large losses and industry trends.

Partner with TPA Governance and Relationship Management to help TPA’s and Insureds comply with claim handling and reporting guidelines.

Work with TPA Claims Financial to check the accuracy of TPA financials ensuring alignment with TTPO financials.

What you will need to succeed

10 plus years of General Liability/Auto claims experience.

Experience with complex and high exposure General Liability Bodily Injury and Property Damage claims.

Excellent communication skills (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills.

Advanced experience and capabilities in litigation claims management, including ADR and mediation processes, involving auto/GL exposures.

Strong technical expertise interpreting insurance contracts.

In depth knowledge of claim handling procedures, claims performance strategies, and claim best practices.

Advanced analytical and problem solving skills.

Should also have a demonstrated ability to initiate and champion change initiatives that leverage technology and improve skills in benchmarking.

Creativity in resolving challenging business problems, as well as ability to achieve business goals and objectives is essential.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Complex Claims Director, TPA Oversight to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

As Complex Claims Director – TPA Oversight, you will analyze and process bodily injury and third-party property damage claims by investigating and gathering information to determine the exposure on the claim; ensure proactive claims handling aimed at the prompt and cost-effective resolution of claims through well-developed action plans. You will determine need for and direct independent adjusters to gather information to determine exposure on the claim and control their costs.

Identify and evaluate coverage issues; prepare comprehensive coverage letters with supervisory review and analysis; retain and provide direction to coverage counsel when necessary.

Assess liability and resolve claim within established evaluation. Maintain diaries and complete tasks within required timeframes as set forth by department guidelines; ensure claim files are timely and properly documented with clear and concise analysis on coverage, damages, reserves, and liability including an action plan for resolution. Process and pay invoices within a timely manner.

Coordinate vendor referrals for additional investigation and/or litigation management. Calculate and assign timely and appropriate reserves; monitor reserve accuracy throughout the life of the claim.

Refer case as appropriate to supervisor and management. Respond to requests or directions in a professional and timely manner.

Attend arbitrations, mediations, settlement conference and trials.

Successfully complete required State licensing examinations and continuing education requirement.

Communicate with all internal business partners including underwriters to make sure underwriting is aware of large losses and industry trends.

Partner with TPA Governance and Relationship Management to help TPA’s and Insureds comply with claim handling and reporting guidelines.

Work with TPA Claims Financial to check the accuracy of TPA financials ensuring alignment with TTPO financials.

What you will need to succeed

7 plus years of General Liability/Auto claims experience.

Experience with complex and high exposure General Liability Bodily Injury and Property Damage claims.

Excellent communication skills (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills.

Advanced experience and capabilities in litigation claims management, including ADR and mediation processes, involving auto/GL exposures.

Strong technical expertise interpreting insurance contracts.

In depth knowledge of claim handling procedures, claims performance strategies, and claim best practices.

Advanced analytical and problem solving skills.

Should also have a demonstrated ability to initiate and champion change initiatives that leverage technology and improve skills in benchmarking.

Creativity in resolving challenging business problems, as well as ability to achieve business goals and objectives is essential.

Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.

The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

Wie zijn wij?

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is een toonaangevende wereldwijde verzekeringsorganisatie. Leer het bedrijf kennen

AIG ontwikkelt verzekeringsoplossingen die de risico's van bedrijven en particulieren afdekken. Wij zijn een innovatieve organisatie en brengen baanbrekende verzekeringsoplossingen op de markt voor onze snel veranderende wereld. Vanuit ons kantoor in het Rivium in Capelle aan den IJssel maak je deel uit van ons Financial Lines team van momenteel 9 enthousiaste professionals.

Over de rol

De rol van Underwriting Analyst Beroepsaansprakelijkheid en Cyber is een dynamische en boeiende functie. Krijg jij energie van het creëren van kansen bij nieuwe klanten en bestaande klanten in het grootzakelijke en multinationale bedrijfssegment? Door over grenzen heen te werken, in gesprek te gaan met grote groepen stakeholders en deel te nemen aan multidisciplinaire deals? En wordt jouw talent optimaal benut door het analyseren en beoordelen van complexe en uitdagende risico's met behulp van geavanceerde analyses en geavanceerde risicoprofileringstechnieken? Aarzel dan niet om contact met ons op te nemen.

Verantwoordelijkheden

Ontwikkelen en onderhouden van een toegewezen portfolio van bestaande Beroepsaansprakelijkheid en Cyber klanten

Zorgen voor het behoud en de behandeling van Beroepsaansprakelijkheid en Cyber - accounts door middel van uitstekende service aan klanten en makelaars, monitoring en verlenging van accounts tegen optimale voorwaarden en indien mogelijk crossselling met andere Financial Lines-producten

Business development van nieuwe (internationale) klanten

Het analyseren van risico's, het uitbrengen van offertes en het onderschrijven van de toegewezen risico’s volgens Beroepsaansprakelijkheid en Cyber productlijnen met een succesvolle realisatie van de toegekende budgetdoelstelling

Bijdrage aan productinnovatie

Bewaken van resultaten, het delen en ontwikkelen van ideeën om de productiviteit en winstgevendheid te verhogen

Efficiënte en tijdige afhandeling van polis uitgifte en accountverwerking, inclusief premie boekingsinstructies, polis opstellen en follow-up met de serviceteams

Het naleven van wettelijke en interne regels en richtlijnen en het spelen van een voorbeeldfunctie hieromtrent naar andere teamleden.

We zijn op zoek naar een startende professional die leergierig is en passie krijgt van het werken in een dynamische internationale omgeving met 's werelds toonaangevende bedrijven. De afhandeling begint vanaf de eerste melding en omvat het beoordelen van polis- en wettelijke aansprakelijkheid, je kwantumanalyse en leidt tot een tijdige en nauwkeurige afwikkeling, terwijl je de kostenrisico's beperkt. Je communiceert ontwikkelingen en uitkomsten indien nodig aan alle belangrijke belanghebbenden (intern en extern) en biedt een hoog serviceniveau aan klanten, terwijl je de Best Practices voor schadeafhandeling en wettelijke, regelgeving en nalevingsvereisten volgt.

Jouw toekomstige team

Stel je voor dat je een succesvolle carrière opbouwt bij AIG, samenwerkend met andere getalenteerde en zeer gemotiveerde collega’s die zich dagelijks inzetten om ons doel te bereiken: de meest toonaangevende verzekeringsmaatschappij ter wereld te worden. Wij geloven dat ons succes afhangt van het hebben van een team van wereldklasse.

 

Jouw verantwoordelijkheden:

Breed intern en extern communiceren met belanghebbenden waar nodig.

Bijdragen aan het onderhoud van Best Practice procedures voor maritieme claims, in lijn met wereldwijde Best Practices.

Afhandelen van maritieme claims die binnen het afgesproken autorisatieniveau vallen.

Terugkoppeling geven van trends in claims analyses aan het team en interne belanghebbenden.

Sterke relaties opbouwen en onderhouden met underwriters en andere relevante zakelijke belanghebbenden in de regio.

Bijwonen van claimsbesprekingen en reizen indien nodig.

Ondersteunen van de Marine Claims Manager bij taken die gericht zijn op claimsprestaties en rapportages indien nodig.

Ondersteunen van de Marine Claims Manager en het bredere team bij ad-hoc projecten indien nodig.

Helpen bij het beheren van de dagelijkse operationele relatie/kwaliteitsborgingskwesties met Shared Services.

Technische begeleiding en coaching bieden aan junior, minder ervaren collega’s van het wereldwijde maritieme claimsteam.

‘Thought leadership’ tonen door middel van training en presentaties aan zowel interne als externe doelgroepen.

Wat we zoeken

Een persoon met uitgebreide ervaring in maritieme verzekeringsclaims.

Kennis van de door Marine gebruikte verzekeringstaal voor nauwkeurige en consistente interpretatie.

Ervaring in het beheren van advocaten, experts en juridische uitgaven.

Vermogen om te presenteren aan cliënten en interne belanghebbenden.

Sterke kennis van juridische, regelgevende en procesmatige vereisten specifiek voor maritieme zaken.

Vermogen om effectief bij te dragen binnen een teamomgeving.

Goede communicatieve vaardigheden.

Goede kennis en ervaring met markt-IT-systemen en geavanceerde vaardigheden in Microsoft-toepassingen.

Iemand die kansen ziet om processen en efficiëntie te verbeteren en in staat is om transformatieprojecten uit te voeren.

Een proactief en zelfstandig persoon.

Aanbod

AIG biedt een concurrerend primair en secundaire arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket op basis van ervaring en functieniveau, vergezeld van andere voordelen zoals wereldwijde carrièremogelijkheden en uitgebreide trainings- en persoonlijke ontwikkelingsprogramma's.

Wie zijn wij

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is een toonaangevende wereldwijde verzekeringsorganisatie. Voortbouwend op 100 jaar ervaring, bieden de branche en partner ondernemingen van AIG vandaag de dag een breed scala aan schadeverzekeringen, levensverzekeringen, pensioenoplossingen en andere financiële diensten aan klanten in meer dan 80 landen en rechtsgebieden. Deze diverse aanbiedingen omvatten producten en diensten die bedrijven en individuen helpen om hun activa te beschermen, risico's te beheersen en voor pensioenzekerheid te zorgen. De Nederlandse organisatie heeft 120 medewerkers waarvan er 35 werkzaam zijn op de schadeafdeling. Je vormt een team van 2 behandelaren die Property schades zullen behandelen. Samen met de collega's van Marine zitten jullie in een team van 6 collega's, de manager en een werkstudent.

Wij zijn een werkgever die gelijke kansen biedt

Het is het beleid van AIG, haar dochterondernemingen en zusterbedrijven nu en voor de toekomst, om een gelijke kansen werkgever te zijn. Wij bieden gelijke kansen aan alle gekwalificeerde individuen, ongeacht ras, kleur, religie, leeftijd, geslacht, genderexpressie, nationale herkomst, handicap of enige andere wettelijk beschermde groep mensen. Bij AIG geloven wij dat diversiteit en inclusie van cruciaal belang zijn voor onze toekomst en onze missie - het creëren van een basis voor een creatieve werkplek die leidt tot innovatie, groei en winstgevendheid. Door een breed scala aan programma's en initiatieven investeren wij in elke werknemer, met als doel ervoor te zorgen dat onze mensen niet alleen als individuen worden gerespecteerd, maar ook werkelijk gewaardeerd worden om hun unieke perspectieven.

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.

 

We’re also committed to making a positive difference for our colleagues and in the communities where we work and live. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

 

Get to know the business

Our Global Sourcing & Procurement Services (GS&PS) colleagues manage all AIG third party spend, ensuring maximized productivity and quality. Our global team includes Category Strategy, Negotiations and Execution, Transformation, Operations, Productivity, Environmental Sustainability, Supplier Diversity, Analytics, Tools, and Program Governance. GS&PS is committed to providing value to our stakeholders through building trust, providing a best-in-class procurement experience, maximizing profit, minimizing risk, and enabling sustainable growth for AIG.

 

About the role

The Senior Director of Governance and Policyis a strategic enterprise leader responsible for designing and operating the governance, policy, and control framework that enables AIG to manage third‑party relationships securely, compliantly, and efficiently throughout the full lifecycle—from sourcing through off‑boarding.

 

This role establishes the strategic foundation, operational model, and controls that embed risk, data security, and compliance considerations into every stage of vendor engagement. The Senior Director partners with senior stakeholders across Legal, Cybersecurity, ERM, Risk, Compliance, and GS&PS to ensure a resilient control environment, strong policy discipline, and consistent lifecycle management across the global supply base.

 

Responsibilities

Strategic Governance & Operating Model Leadership

Establish and lead a federated governance model with centralized oversight, clearly defined roles and responsibilities (RACI), and strong cross‑functional accountability.

Develop the governance framework supporting transparent, data‑driven decisions across third‑party lifecycle management.

Define and lead KPIs, performance dashboards, and risk metrics that drive discipline, early‑warning visibility, and continuous improvement.

Advise senior leadership on governance best practices, regulatory expectations, and emerging operational risks.

Policy Strategy, Standards & Control Framework

Own the GS&PS policy and standards framework, ensuring alignment with enterprise policies, regulatory expectations, and contractual requirements.

Formalize and embed third‑party data protection, cybersecurity, and operational control requirements into sourcing, contracting, supplier onboarding, and ongoing vendor management.

Lead policy lifecycle management—including drafting, review, approvals, version control, training, and enterprise‑wide communication.

Build and deliver training and awareness programs that elevate risk, data security, and policy understanding across business and procurement teams.

Process Optimization, Standardization & Automation

Champion operational excellence using Lean Six Sigma, business process management (BPM), and automation opportunities.

Design and implement scalable, efficient processes that embed controls and compliance expectations into frontline procurement activities.

Lead change management, training, and adoption programs to ensure new processes and technologies deliver intended outcomes.

Monitor adherence to approved processes and drive continuous refinement based on performance data, audit findings, and regulatory changes.

Audit, Regulatory Alignment & Executive Engagement

Serve as the primary GS&PS leader for audit readiness, regulatory exams, and internal/external reviews involving third‑party governance and controls.

Ensure timely and accurate fulfillment of requests and execution of remediation plans.

Communicate complex governance, risk, and policy topics clearly for executive and board‑level audiences.

Provide strategic thought leadership and influence to shape enterprise decision‑making related to third‑party risks, security, and operational resiliency.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Risk, Cybersecurity, or related field; Master’s degree, JD, or advanced certifications (e.g., PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Prosci, CTPRP) preferred. 

10+ years of senior leadership experience in governance, policy, risk, cybersecurity, compliance, or procurement within complex, regulated environments. 

Proven ability to design and operationalize enterprise governance frameworks, including roles, decision structures, KPIs, and executive reporting.

Strong executive communication and influencing skills, with the ability to simplify complex risk and policy issues for senior leaders and drive cross‑functional alignment. 

Demonstrated experience in process optimization and control integration using methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, or BPM. 

Risk‑ and controls‑oriented mindset, with the ability to identify gaps, lead remediation, and partner effectively with Cybersecurity, Legal, ERM, and Compliance. 

Proven track record supporting audit readiness, regulatory exams, and remediation management. 

Strong organizational leadership with the ability to lead change, guide matrixed teams, and drive enterprise‑wide adoption of governance and policy requirements. 

Data‑driven decision maker with strong business acumen and the ability to balance risk, operational efficiency, and strategic objectives.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Multinational
AIG’s Multinational business is an exciting area that provides multinational insurance solutions for our global customers, empowering them to navigate their cross-border risks with confidence and consistency. AIG Multinational professionals have the diverse skills and expertise necessary to deliver customized, compliant and seamless solutions that support our clients’ risk management objectives. You can work alongside a dynamic, multi-disciplinary team to explore new opportunities for customers.

About the role
The Head of Multinational, Canada will provide leadership and strategic direction of AIG’s Multinational business across Canada and participate in the Multinational North America Leadership Team, working to expand AIG’s Multinational presence by optimizing alignment, integration, adoption and execution of AIG’s global multinational strategies, business plans, operating model and segmented value proposition(s), in support of profitable growth.
This role reports directly to the Head of Multinational, North America.

How you will create an impact

Support the Head of Multinational, North America through active participation and contribution to the leadership and direction of AIG’s multinational business.

Work with AIG Canada leadership & stakeholders to foster alignment, integration, & execution of agreed multinational business model(s) and segmented multinational value proposition.

Manage a team of Multinational Client Executives and Multinational Client Coordinators in alignment with AIG’s Global Multinational Business Model, to deliver superior Multinational client service and stakeholder experience.

Drive the multinational vision, value proposition and execution of the multinational strategic plan across the full spectrum of general insurance products in Canada, ensuring expert design and management of global fronting and multinational programs and world class service to our global clients and broker partners.

Partner in driving the execution of the profitable growth of the multinational portfolio including pipeline management and development & execution of specific multinational sales, marketing and communications strategies in conjunction with Product, Distribution and AIG Canada leadership.

Effectively manage and drive the profitable growth and servicing of the AIG Canada produced complex global fronting portfolio in alignment with transforming Target Operation Model (TOM), ensuring adherence to our global fronting underwriting, credit, pricing, reinsurance, and legal practices.

Represent AIG Multinational as a visible and recognized thought and industry leader. Internally, be an expert on fronting and multinational business including program design, structuring, regulation, and the multinational end-to-end process. Externally, develop relationships with key Canada clients and broker partners, and participate at insurance related events including panels, leading workshops, speaking engagements, etc. This includes production of thought leadership articles and white papers.

Lead change in behavior and practice across the Canada Multinational team to manage and support producing office business/service on an end to end (E2E) basis, leveraging all AIG MN/Network capabilities, resources and reports.

Deliver on all KPIs on customer service, profitability, and expense management across the AIG Canada produced multinational portfolio.

Lead the adoption & execution of the multinational business model (including E2E Processes) and promotion of the segmented multinational value proposition(s) both internally across Canada multinational and with clients and broker partners to deliver a globally consistent client experience and contract certainty.

Work with claims to ensure multinational claims are handled in a proactive manner, ensuring claims stands out as a competitive differentiator for AIG.

Create a risk-aware culture of integrity and accountability to ensure full awareness and compliance of AIG policies and procedures, ethical behaviours and practices, and ownership of risks in day-to-day responsibilities.

Foster an environment where employees can grow and maximize their talent including appropriate training, career development, and succession planning. Through regular governance, evaluate staff knowledge, skill gaps, training needs, and career development and deliver plans to address these needs ensuring continuous knowledge improvement and staff advancement.

Support the Multinational transformation agenda and own agreed deliverables for Canada’s Multinational produced business. Collaborate with business leaders and stakeholders to address critical end-to-end business and operating model challenges related to structure, business process, underwriting, service pricing models, and claims. 

What you’ll need to succeed

10+ years of insurance experience in positions of increasing authority, including significant experience handling large client relationships and at least 5 years managing a sales and/or service-oriented workforce of varying levels. Strong and deep multinational knowledge.

Inspiring leader able to attract, engage, retain, and develop a high performing team to meet current and future business needs with ability to clearly articulate a strategic vision and execute the plan.

Knowledge of fronting and multinational business across multiple lines of business in multiple markets, including structuring, credit, reinsurance, financial, legal and regulatory aspects.

Proven successful management of complex, multi-stakeholder team(s) through periods of significant change.

Excellent influencing and communications skills including effective engagement with senior level managers across multiple levels and areas of the company, and externally with key clients and broker partners.

Demonstrated change agent able to identify and implement operational and process improvements.

Process orientated to implement change and continuously review and identify process improvements to gain efficiencies.
